title: Square a racked wooden frame with a diagonal clamp
instruction: Square the wooden frame with the diagonal clamp. Leave the clamp in place and release both hands.
setup: A loose four-rail timber frame with 400 by 300 mm joint-center spacing rests on a 600 by 720 mm mat. Four 28 mm round corner blocks mark the joints. The initial corner error is 7 degrees. A free steel-bar sliding clamp lies 105 mm to one side with an open span and two orange grip pads. The YAM hands start open.
scoring: 0.25 for handling the clamp, moving both ends at least 60 mm from rest and seating both faces on the initially longer diagonal. 0.50 after narrowing the span a further 5 mm or more and at least halving the initial diagonal difference with both jaws seated. 1.00 after the seated clamp holds the diagonals within 1 mm and all corners within 0.2 degrees of square for three continuous seconds with both open hands clear.
context: A dry-fit cabinet frame must be squared before its joints are fixed. Diagonal clamping changes its shape as the two diagonal measurements converge. A May 2025 US national estimate counted 670,090 carpenters. Building and repairing cabinets and frameworks is an O*NET task for carpenters (47-2031.00).
fidelity: Four rigid rails rotate about ideal corner pins. The slider has passive velocity-dependent drag and the frame rests on a frictional mat. Joint compliance, glue curing, wood deformation and commercial clamp holding force are uncalibrated.
reset_notes: Fixed layout, seed 0. Start a fresh environment, restore all poses and joint limits, and settle for 30 control frames.
scores: Seed 0: Dream-1 scored 0.00 in 800 steps (40.00 s; step_limit). Scripted YAM scored 1.00 in 643 steps (32.15 s; success).
